quote: Let Xi ~ GZD(thetai), i = 1, 2 be two random variables. If theta1 >= theta2, then X1 ≺lr X2, X1 ≺hr X2, X1 ≺s X2 and X1 <=cx X2. Proof. We have fX1(t)/fX2(t) = (sum_{k=0}^n ak k!/theta2^{k+1})/(sum_{k=0}^n ak k!/theta1^{k+1}) * e^{-(theta1 - theta2) t}. For simplification, we use ln(fX1(t)/fX2(t)). Now, we can find d/dt ln(fX1(t)/fX2(t)) = -(theta1 - theta2). To this end, if theta1 >= theta2, we have d/dt ln(fX1(t)/fX2(t)) <= 0. This means that X1 ≺lr X2. Also, according to Remark 3 the theorem is proved.
family: generalized zero-truncated distribution GZD(theta): f(t) = (sum_{k=0}^n a_k t^k) e^{-theta t} / (sum_{k=0}^n a_k k!/theta^{k+1}), theta > 0, coefficients a_k >= 0
compared: two GZD variables differing only in theta

hypotheses.formal: same coefficient vector (a_0,...,a_n); only theta differs

conclusion.direction: X1 ≺lr X2 (theta1 >= theta2 implies X1 smaller in lr)

ambiguity: Directly proved via d/dt log pdf-ratio = -(theta1 - theta2) <= 0; the paper's definition d) has X ≺lr Y iff f_Y/f_X decreasing — note the proof differentiates fX1/fX2 and concludes X1 ≺lr X2 with the ratio fX1/fX2 decreasing (equivalent formulation).
